incidents.title: Drones strike cargo ship Chelsea 3 off Byala, Bulgaria; crew of 15 rescued
incidents.place: Black Sea, about 18 nautical miles east of Byala (Bulgarian exclusive economic zone)
incidents.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the Maltese-flagged cargo ship Chelsea 3 was hit by three aerial drones about 18 nautical miles east of Byala, in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea, during the night of 12 to 13 October 2026. All 15 crew members were rescued.
incidents.impact: The Border Police rescued all 15 crew members (seven Ukrainian and eight Azerbaijani nationals) and took them to Varna; five received treatment for minor injuries, according to BTA and BNT, while Sega reports six hurt, mostly with light burns. The ship, sailing empty from Giresun (Türkiye) to Giurgiulești (Moldova), stayed afloat and was at anchor.
incidents.evidence: Drone involvement rests on the statement of Bulgaria's prime minister, whose country is not a party to the war, and on the crew, who described three strikes on the deck and side. The national news agency BTA and the public broadcaster BNT report the statement; Sega adds the ship's route and management. A distress signal reached Bulgaria's maritime rescue centre at about 01:30 (Sega: 01:57). Sources give the distance as 15 or 18 nautical miles off Byala.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones and from where is not established. The exact time of the strike is not given in the cited sources.
incidents.attribution: Not established. Radev said there was no solid, clear evidence against any party, while arguing that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation; he said he would summon Russia's ambassador for talks.

incidents.place: Black Sea, about 17 nautical miles east of Krapets (Bulgarian exclusive economic zone)
incidents.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said a second merchant ship was hit and sank about 17 nautical miles east of Krapets in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, in the same series of drone attacks in which the Chelsea 3 was struck off Byala on the night of 12 to 13 October 2026. President Iliana Iotova identified the sunken ship as the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity. Early reports had named the Azov Concord; Sega later reported that the Azov Concord had helped in the rescue.
incidents.impact: The ship sank. Bulgarian officials said five crew members were rescued and 11 were missing; the prime minister had first reported one crew member rescued. According to Sega, the HS Dignity had a crew of 16 and was sailing without cargo from Algeria to Braila, Romania.
incidents.evidence: Reported by Bulgaria's prime minister, whose country is not a party to the war, as one of the ships hit in the night's drone attacks; the ship was identified by President Iliana Iotova. Carried by the national news agency BTA, the public broadcaster BNT, Sega and Al Jazeera. The number of drones that hit this ship is not given.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones and how many hit the ship were not clear at the time of reporting. Sega places the sinking 17 miles east of Shabla rather than Krapets.
incidents.attribution: Not established. Radev said there was no solid, clear evidence against any party, while arguing that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation; he said he would summon Russia's ambassador for talks.

incidents.title: Drone strike near displacement camp in Sudan's Blue Nile kills at least 30, officials say
incidents.summary: A drone strike on Friday 9 October hit the centre of Wad al-Mahi province in Sudan's Blue Nile region, just outside a displacement camp. The provincial governor said it killed 26 women and four children; a group that tracks the war later put the toll at at least 40, including children.
incidents.impact: The governor of Wad al-Mahi province told Al Jazeera that 30 people were killed, 26 women and four children, and dozens were wounded. Emergency Lawyers, a group that tracks the war, said at least 40 people were killed in the Abu Shandi area. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said it was appalled by the strike.
incidents.evidence: The death toll differs between sources: at least 30 according to the provincial governor, at least 40 according to Emergency Lawyers as reported by the Associated Press. The strike was reported near an informal gold mining site where displaced women work.
incidents.unknown: The exact number of victims, the type of drone and where it was launched from are not independently established in the cited sources.
incidents.attribution: The governor said the drone belonged to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and was launched from inside Ethiopia; Emergency Lawyers also said the RSF was responsible. Ethiopia has denied harbouring RSF fighters. The Sudanese government also held the RSF responsible, according to the Syrian state news agency SANA. No response from the RSF is included in the cited sources.

incidents.title: Riyadh airport attacked; Houthis say they used ballistic missiles and drones
incidents.summary: Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority (GACA) said one person was killed and eight wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 6 or 7 October. The Houthi military spokesperson said the group attacked Saudi airports with ballistic missiles and drones.
incidents.impact: GACA reported one person killed, a resident of Sudanese nationality, and eight wounded at King Khalid International Airport.
incidents.evidence: The casualty figures come from a statement by the Saudi civil aviation authority, GACA, as reported by the BBC. 'Impact confirmed' refers to those officially reported casualties at the airport; it does not establish that drones caused them. incidents.title: Russian drones enter Polish airspace overnight; Poland and NATO allies shoot some down
incidents.place: Eastern and central Poland, including the Lublin region
incidents.summary: Overnight on 9 to 10 September 2025, drones entered Polish airspace during a Russian wave of strikes on Ukraine. Poland's prime minister told parliament that 19 violations were recorded over seven hours. Polish and Dutch aircraft, supported by other NATO assets, shot down some of the drones. Poland called it an act of aggression and consulted allies under Article 4 of the NATO treaty.
incidents.impact: Part of Poland's airspace was closed for several hours and Warsaw's Chopin Airport suspended flights. A house in the village of Wyryki in the Lublin region was damaged and its roof largely torn off; the people inside were not hurt. Drones were found at seven locations, and objects of unknown origin at an eighth.
incidents.evidence: Polish authorities recorded the violations and recovered drones at multiple sites, and a NATO spokesman said NATO planes engaged potential threats in allied airspace. Figures differ between sources: 19 violations over seven hours according to the prime minister on 10 September, and 21 drones detected with at least three shot down in the Arms Control Association's later summary.
incidents.unknown: Whether the incursion was intentional. Russia's Defense Ministry said it did not target Poland, and Belarus said it tracked drones that lost their course after jamming, while several European leaders said it appeared intentional. The exact number of drones and of those shot down is not settled, and the cause of the damage to the house (drone debris or an interceptor) is described differently.
incidents.attribution: Polish authorities and NATO officials treated the drones as Russian, and the Arms Control Association reports that debris analysis by multiple media outlets and Polish authorities indicates Russian origin, likely Gerbera-type drones. A joint statement by the foreign ministers of Poland, Lithuania and Ukraine on 12 September accused Russia of a deliberate and coordinated strike. Russia denied targeting Poland, so responsibility for sending the drones into Polish airspace, and intent, remain disputed; recorded here as suspected.

claims.statement: Poland's prime minister told parliament that 19 airspace violations were recorded over seven hours.
claims.quote: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told parliament 19 violations were recorded over seven hours, but that information was still being gathered.
claims.note: Preliminary official figure, described as not final; the Arms Control Association later cites 21 drones.

claims.statement: A NATO spokesman said it was the first time NATO planes had engaged potential threats in allied airspace.
claims.quote: the first time NATO planes have engaged potential threats in Allied airspace
claims.note: Confirmation of an allied engagement by NATO itself, not only by Poland.

claims.statement: The mayor of Wyryki said a house was hit and much of its roof ripped off, with nobody hurt.
claims.quote: told TVP Info that a house was hit. Much of the roof was ripped off. He said people were inside but nobody was hurt.
claims.note: Local official. The Arms Control Association says falling debris, likely from a NATO interceptor, damaged the house.

claims.statement: The Arms Control Association says debris analysis by media outlets and Polish authorities confirms the aircraft are of Russian origin, likely Gerbera-type drones.
claims.quote: visual analysis of debris by multiple media outlets and Polish authorities confirm the aircraft are of Russian origin, likely Gerbera-type drones that can be equipped either as decoys or with explosive charges
claims.note: Independent summary of origin. Origin is not the same as intent, which remains disputed.

claims.note: A denial of intent by parties with an interest in the outcome; it does not dispute Russian origin of the drones.

incidents.title: Drone launched from Yemen strikes arrivals hall at Ramon Airport near Eilat; Houthis claim attack
incidents.summary: On Sunday 7 September 2025 a drone launched from Yemen struck the arrivals hall at Israel's Ramon Airport near the Red Sea city of Eilat, injuring two people and halting takeoffs and landings for about two hours. The Houthis claimed responsibility. The Israeli military said its systems detected the drone but did not classify it as hostile, so interception and alert systems were not activated.
incidents.impact: Takeoffs and landings were halted for around two hours and the airport later reopened for full operations. Israel's ambulance service said a 63-year-old man was injured by shrapnel and a 52-year-old woman was hurt, with Haaretz reporting she was injured after she fell; others received treatment for panic attacks. Airline Arkia said its aircraft were undamaged.
incidents.evidence: The Israeli military, the Airports Authority and the national ambulance service all described a drone from Yemen that fell in the arrivals hall area, and the Houthi spokesperson claimed the strike. Israeli Army Radio reported that a preliminary investigation indicated the drone had not been spotted by the air force's detection systems at all, which differs from the military's statement that it was detected but not classified as hostile.
incidents.unknown: How the drone evaded classification as a threat, the drone type, and whether other drones in the Houthi operation reached southern Israel; the military said it had intercepted three drones launched from Yemen and did not elaborate on the status of the third.
incidents.attribution: The Houthi military spokesperson claimed that a drone directly hit the airport and said airports inside occupied Palestine would be continuously targeted. Israel's military said the drone was launched from Yemen.

incidents.title: Drone strikes hit Port Sudan over several days, damaging fuel depots, the airport and the main power substation
incidents.summary: From 4 May 2025 drones struck military and civilian sites in Port Sudan, the army-aligned government's wartime base on the Red Sea, over several days. Reported targets include a military base near the airport, fuel depots, the airport, a hotel near the presidential residence and the city's main power substation. Military sources blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which did not claim the attacks.
incidents.impact: Fuel depots burned, air traffic was halted on 6 May at the only airport still handling international civilian flights, and a strike on the main power substation caused a blackout across the city. The maritime security firm Ambrey reported drone strikes on the container terminal. No immediate reports of casualties were given in the AFP report. Nearly all humanitarian aid into Sudan arrives through Port Sudan, and the UN chief called the reports of attacks a worrying development.
incidents.evidence: Officials of the national electricity company and the airport confirmed drone hits, AFP and Reuters correspondents or witnesses reported explosions and smoke, and Ambrey reported drone strikes on the container terminal. Blame for the strikes rests on military sources and residents, not on a claim of responsibility or an independent investigation.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones and from where, the type of drones, and the full extent of damage and casualties. The RSF's statement did not address the attacks. Sudan's army-aligned government accused the UAE of supplying the drones to the RSF; the UAE has consistently denied backing the RSF.
incidents.attribution: Sudanese military sources blamed the RSF, and residents told Al Jazeera they believed RSF drone strikes were responsible. The RSF did not address the attacks in a statement late on 6 May. Sudan's army-aligned government severed diplomatic relations with the UAE over alleged arming of the RSF. None of this has been independently established.

incidents.title: Drone strike damages the Chornobyl New Safe Confinement; IAEA later finds it lost its confinement function
incidents.place: Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant, Kyiv region
incidents.summary: At about 01:50 on 14 February 2025 a drone struck the New Safe Confinement, the structure covering the destroyed Unit 4 reactor at the Chornobyl site, and caused a fire. The IAEA team at the site heard the explosion and saw a breach of the outer layer. In late 2025 the IAEA reported that the strike caused significant structural damage and that the structure had lost its primary safety functions, including confinement, without permanent damage to its load-bearing structures.
incidents.impact: No casualties were reported and radiation levels inside and outside the building stayed normal and stable. The IAEA later said the strike did not lead to any release of radioactive material but caused significant structural damage affecting the confinement function and projected lifetime of the structure. Limited temporary repairs were carried out on the roof, and further temporary repairs were planned for 2026 with support from the EBRD.
incidents.evidence: The IAEA team at the site heard the explosion, saw smoke, fire and the breach, and was informed by Ukraine that a drone had struck the structure. The IAEA's later statements describe the event as a drone strike, and its comprehensive safety assessment confirmed the loss of confinement capability. The IAEA did not attribute the strike.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drone: AP reported that it was not possible to independently confirm who was behind the strike. The IAEA statements in the cited sources do not state the drone type.
incidents.attribution: Ukraine's president said a Russian drone with a high-explosive warhead hit the shell. A Kremlin spokesman denied the claim, saying Russia's military does not strike nuclear facilities. The IAEA did not attribute blame.

incidents.title: Drone strikes on Tinzaouaten in northern Mali: rebel coalition says 21 civilians killed, army confirms airstrikes
incidents.summary: On 25 August 2024, airstrikes hit the village of Tinzaouatine (Tinzaouaten) in northern Mali near the Algerian border. A coalition of Tuareg-majority groups fighting for independence said drones hit a pharmacy and then people gathering nearby, killing at least 21 civilians including 11 children. Mali's General Staff confirmed airstrikes in the sector and said the precision strikes targeted terrorists.

The Associated Press described it as the largest number of civilians killed by drones since the peace agreement between the junta and pro-independence groups broke down in 2023.

incidents.title: Houthi-claimed drone strikes central Tel Aviv, killing one person; Israeli military cites human error
incidents.place: Tel Aviv (neighbourhood near the US Embassy)
incidents.summary: At around 3:10 a.m. on 19 July 2024 an explosive drone struck central Tel Aviv, killing one person and wounding others in a neighbourhood near the US Embassy. The Houthis in Yemen claimed responsibility. Israel's military said it believed the drone was an upgraded Iranian Samad-3 that had flown from Yemen, and an Israeli military official said it was identified but penetrated Israel because of human error in operating the system.
incidents.impact: Israel's emergency services said the body of a 50-year-old man was found in an apartment close to the explosion and four people were taken to hospital with slight shrapnel injuries; AP reported at least 10 wounded, citing local police. The blast blew out windows and damaged cars over a wide area. It was described as the first lethal Houthi attack in Israel.
incidents.evidence: Israeli police and emergency services reported the casualties, and the Israeli military described the drone type and its approach from Yemen. The drone type rests on an Israeli military assessment; Israeli media reported that fragments of a drone of a kind widely used by Iranian-backed groups were recovered, and the military had not determined whether it exploded in the air or struck a building.
incidents.unknown: Whether the drone exploded in the air or hit a building, the exact number of injured (four slightly wounded in Reuters, at least 10 in AP), and the cause of the failure to sound alarms, which the military is investigating. The Houthis' claim of a new drone capable of bypassing defences was rebuffed by the Israeli military.
incidents.attribution: The Houthi spokesperson claimed responsibility on X and said the strike used a new drone called Yafa. Israel's military said it believed the drone arrived from Yemen. Analysts and Western intelligence services have long accused Iran of arming the Houthis, which Tehran denies.

incidents.title: Drone attacks hit Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, including a reactor building, IAEA says
incidents.place: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar area
incidents.summary: On 7 April 2024 drones struck the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, the first direct targeting of the plant since November 2022 according to the IAEA. The IAEA's director general reported at least three direct hits against the main reactor containment structures, and on 9 April another drone detonated on the roof of the plant's training centre outside the site perimeter. Russia and Ukraine blamed each other.
incidents.impact: The IAEA said damage at unit 6 did not compromise nuclear safety but was a serious incident with potential to undermine the integrity of the reactor's containment system, and one casualty was reported. Russia's state nuclear agency said three people were wounded. The plant's six reactors had been shut down for months.
incidents.evidence: IAEA experts at the plant verified the impact of several drone attacks on 7 April, and on 9 April they heard a loud explosion at the time the plant said a drone detonated on the training centre roof. The IAEA team was denied access to several locations for security reasons. The director general later told the IAEA Board the strike did not compromise nuclear safety in a serious way.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the drones and from where: the IAEA did not attribute the attacks. The drone type is not stated in the cited sources. The IAEA could not visit several of the locations where the plant reported attacks.
incidents.attribution: Plant officials said Ukrainian military drones carried out the attack, and Russia's IAEA ambassador accused the agency of being afraid to say Ukraine was behind it. Ukraine's UN ambassador called the strike a false flag operation by Russia. The IAEA director general said that whoever is behind the attacks is playing with fire and did not attribute them.

incidents.title: Anti-junta forces say 29 drones targeted Naypyidaw military sites; junta says it shot down seven
incidents.place: Naypyidaw (military headquarters, Aye Lar air base and Naypyidaw International Airport)
incidents.summary: On the morning of 4 April 2024 anti-junta forces attacked the Myanmar capital Naypyidaw with drones in a rare strike on the military regime's stronghold. The shadow National Unity Government said 29 explosive-laden drones targeted the military headquarters and an air base. The junta said its air defences shot down seven drones near the airport and a township and that there was no damage or casualties.
incidents.impact: Accounts conflict. The National Unity Government said preliminary reports indicated there were casualties, while the junta said there was no damage or casualties. incidents.evidence: The attack is described by both sides: the junta displayed images of downed drones and said it had seized 13, and anti-junta groups published photos of the drones used. Casualty and damage claims come from the parties and are not independently verified; residents near the targeted sites told RFA they were unaware of the attacks.
incidents.unknown: How many drones were launched, whether any reached their targets, and whether anyone was hurt. The numbers claimed by the sides (29 launched; seven shot down; 13 seized) cannot be reconciled from the cited sources.
incidents.attribution: The shadow National Unity Government and the anti-junta Shar Htoo Waw's Kloud Drone Team, working with units of the People's Defence Force, claimed the attack. The junta did not name who launched the drones in the statements cited.

incidents.title: Three US service members killed in one-way drone attack on Tower 22 outpost in northeast Jordan
incidents.place: Tower 22 logistics outpost, northeast Jordan near the Syrian border
incidents.summary: On 28 January 2024 a one-way attack drone struck a US logistics outpost known as Tower 22 in northeast Jordan, near the Syrian border. US Central Command said three US service members were killed and at least 34 were injured. It was the first attack on US forces in Jordan since the Israel-Hamas war began and the first in the region to kill US troops since then.
incidents.impact: CENTCOM said three US service members were killed and at least 34 injured, with eight evacuated from Jordan in stable condition; about 350 US Army and Air Force personnel were deployed at the base. Jordan's government said none of its own troops were hurt.
incidents.evidence: CENTCOM described a one-way attack UAS that impacted the base, and Jordan's government spokesperson said the attack was carried out by a drone. Reporting says it is unclear why air defences did not intercept the drone. The outpost is not publicly disclosed by Jordan.
incidents.unknown: Which group launched the drone and from where, and why it was not intercepted. The injury figure was expected to fluctuate as personnel received follow-on care.
incidents.attribution: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, a network of Iranian-backed Iraqi militias, claimed credit for the attack, according to Task & Purpose; The War Zone reports the group said it attacked other US bases in Syria and an Israeli naval facility, without naming Tower 22 in the statement it quotes. The US president said the attack was carried out by radical Iran-backed militant groups operating in Syria and Iraq and did not name a specific group.

claims.quote: On Jan. 28, three U.S. service members were killed, and multiple personnel were injured from a one-way attack UAS that impacted on a base in northeast Jordan, near the Syrian border.
claims.note: Official statement as reproduced by The War Zone; the basis for the confirmed drone status together with Jordan's statement.

claims.note: Updated official figure; an earlier report said 25 injured.

incidents.title: Nigerian military drone strike kills villagers at a religious gathering in Tudun Biri, Kaduna state
incidents.place: Tudun Biri village, Igabi area, Kaduna state
incidents.summary: A drone strike on the night of Sunday 3 December 2023 hit villagers gathered in Tudun Biri, in Kaduna state's Igabi area, to mark the Prophet Muhammad's birthday. Kaduna's governor said civilians were mistakenly killed by a drone targeting terrorists and bandits, and the army division commander was quoted as saying a routine army mission inadvertently affected community members. The president ordered an investigation.
incidents.impact: The National Emergency Management Agency said 85 bodies had been buried while the search continued. Amnesty International's Nigeria office said 120 people were killed, citing its workers and volunteers; VOA reported at least 87 killed and at least 60 injured. Dozens of wounded were evacuated for treatment.
incidents.evidence: Kaduna state officials and the army division commander, as quoted in a state ministry statement, described a mistaken drone strike during an army operation. The Nigerian Air Force said it carried out no operations in Kaduna that night and noted it is not the only force operating armed drones. Defence officials later said terrorists had embedded themselves in the village, which the governor criticised.
incidents.unknown: The final death toll (85 buried per the emergency agency, at least 87 per later reporting, 120 per Amnesty), the circumstances of the targeting error, and the findings of the presidential investigation. A Nigerian army spokesperson had not responded to requests for comment in the first reports.
incidents.attribution: The head of the army division in Kaduna was quoted by the state government as saying the army was on a routine mission against terrorists and inadvertently affected members of the community, and the governor described a drone targeting terrorists and bandits. The air force said it did not operate in Kaduna that night. Amnesty International accused authorities of putting out contradictory explanations.

claims.statement: The National Emergency Management Agency said 85 bodies had been buried while the search was ongoing.
claims.quote: 85 dead bodies have so far been buried while search is still ongoing
claims.note: Official figure on the day; later reporting by VOA gives at least 87 killed.

claims.statement: Amnesty International's Nigeria office said 120 people were killed.
claims.quote: Amnesty International’s Nigeria office said 120 people were killed in the attack, citing reports of its workers and volunteers in the area

incidents.impact: The Saudi Press Agency, citing the interior ministry, said Aramco's industrial security teams were dealing with fires at both sites, which were later reported under control. Saudi Arabia said on 3 October that it had fully restored oil output.
incidents.evidence: The use of drones rests on the Saudi interior ministry's statement, the Houthi claim and the UN monitors' report, which refers to drones and land-attack cruise missiles used on 14 September. The production figure comes from unnamed sources cited by Reuters rather than an official statement.
incidents.unknown: Who launched the attack and from where. The monitors were not tasked with identifying who was responsible.
incidents.attribution: The Houthis claimed responsibility. The United States, European countries and Saudi Arabia accused Iran, which denied involvement.
